summary.oneLiner: Indigo Paints is a Pune-headquartered decorative paints company that has built a national challenger position over twenty-five years through category-first differentiated products spanning paints, waterproofing and construction chemicals.
summary.business: Indigo Paints Limited, incorporated in 2000 and headquartered in Pune, manufactures and sells decorative paints and allied products in India. Its portfolio spans interior and exterior emulsions, enamels, wood coatings, primers, putties, distempers, cement paints, waterproofing solutions and construction chemicals, serving residential, commercial and institutional requirements. Products reach the market through an expanding dealer network, depot infrastructure and an installed tinting-machine base, supported by manufacturing facilities in Rajasthan, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

currentContext.strengths: Differentiated, category-first portfolio - described as India's first metallic paint, India's first floor coat paint, a first-of-its-kind tile coat paint and a unique ceiling coat paint - which the Company credits for holding the pole position on gross margin in the industry|Gross margin reaching 46.9% in FY26, attributed to the basket of differentiated products and a prudent material purchase policy|Distribution reach of 19,352 active dealers, 55 depots and 12,129 installed tinting machines, all expanded during FY26, plus 16 Indigo Colour Canvas experiential stores|Sustained brand communication has made products such as PU Enamel, Floor Coat, Tile Coat and Dirtproof and Waterproof Exterior Laminate strongly associated with the Indigo brand|Zero-debt on a standalone basis, with the only consolidated borrowing sitting at subsidiary Apple Chemie India Private Limited|Broadened building-solutions platform through the majority stake in Apple Chemie, adding waterproofing and construction chemicals capability and institutional/infrastructure customer reach
currentContext.strategies: Capture market opportunities: accelerate growth and strengthen competitive position through sharper market execution, wider product adoption and expanding presence across priority markets, with the stated aim of growing ahead of the market in FY2026-27|Scale high-potential categories: raise the contribution from premium paints, waterproofing and construction chemicals by improving product adoption and scaling differentiated, application-led solutions|Drive network productivity: increase throughput and wallet share across the active dealer network through better portfolio availability, stronger influencer engagement and focused market execution, rather than reach expansion alone|Unlock operating leverage: with the expanded manufacturing platform largely in place, focus on capacity utilisation, operational efficiency and cash generation as volumes scale, with the current capacity platform expected to support growth for three to four years without significant expansion capex|Expand presence across underpenetrated geographies - a strong Tier 3 and Tier 4 base while continuing to build in Tier 1 and Tier 2 markets - alongside the Indigo Colour Canvas Stores retail format|Grow responsibly: strengthen environmental performance, workplace safety, ethical conduct and accountability, supported by science-based targets, renewable-energy investments and ESG integration into leadership processes|Build the building-solutions platform through Apple Chemie, the construction chemicals subsidiary, which is expanding reach across Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and parts of East and Northeast India|Complete and leverage the capacity augmentation programme, with the new water-based facility at Jodhpur expected to enhance manufacturing flexibility, improve service levels and support growth across northern and eastern markets
currentContext.expansion: The capacity augmentation programme has been substantially completed. Two major capacity initiatives were finished during FY26 at Jodhpur, Rajasthan: a new solvent-based paint facility with a capacity of 12,000 KLPA was commissioned during FY2025-26, and putty manufacturing capacity was doubled from 1,38,000 MT to 2,76,000 MT. The remaining project is the Jodhpur water-based paint facility, which was in the final stages of commissioning at year-end with trial production scheduled to commence in H1 FY2026-27; the Company states that with the commissioning of the water-based plant it will have sufficient capacity to meet growing demand in the near future, and expects the facility to enhance manufacturing flexibility, improve service levels and support growth across northern and eastern markets. On the business-model page the Company sets out existing capacity of 1,72,000 KLPA plus 2,76,000 MTPA, rising to 2,62,000 KLPA plus 2,76,000 MTPA with new launches. The footprint stands at 6 manufacturing plants (existing plants shown at Kochi in Kerala, Pudukkottai in Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan, with Jodhpur marked as the upcoming plant), 55 depots and presence across 36 states and union territories. Beyond paints, subsidiary Apple Chemie India Pvt. Ltd. commissioned a new sealant manufacturing facility at Nagpur during FY2025-26, expanding the specialised construction chemicals platform for institutional, infrastructure and industrial customers. Management states the Company is well positioned to support future demand without significant near-term capital expenditure. On the sustainability side, BRSR Principle 2 reports that 1.67% of total capex in FY2025-26 went into technologies improving environmental and social impacts, against nil in FY2024-25, attributed to 330 kW of solar energy installed at the Kochi facility.

risks.note: Management states that raw material cost volatility remains a near-term consideration, to be mitigated by industry price corrections and internal efficiency measures. The cost of raw materials and components consumed rose faster than the Company would like relative to demand, and input costs are the single largest swing factor on the gross margin the Company describes as its pole position in the industry.

risks.risk: Weak demand and the need to discount to move volume
risks.note: The MD&A records a muted demand environment that warranted relatively higher discounts in the trade channel to spur demand, which affected gross margins marginally. Discounting is the visible transmission channel from soft industry demand to realisations, and it recurs whenever demand softens.

risks.risk: Execution and ramp-up risk on the Jodhpur water-based facility
risks.note: Capital work in progress increased significantly during the year and pertains to the new manufacturing facilities being set up at Jodhpur, Rajasthan for water-based paint products, with commissioning expected in FY2026-27. Until the plant is commissioned and ramped, capital is tied up in work in progress rather than generating output, so any slippage in the FY2026-27 commissioning timeline defers the return on that investment.

Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative implications: water is a primary raw material in the manufacture of water-based paints and its availability is restricted. Mitigation is rainwater harvesting at all factories and a water-recharging pond at one factory premises - a constraint that grows as the water-based capacity base expands.

risks.risk: Energy consumption and dependence on fossil-fuel electricity
risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as both risk and opportunity with negative implications: electricity is a key input to run the factories and excess use of fossil-fuel-generated power impacts the environment. The Company is implementing renewable generation, having commissioned 20 kW of solar at Pune and installed 330 kW of solar capacity at the Kochi facility.

Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative implications: all stakeholder engagements including billing and purchasing run through ERP systems, posing digital and cybersecurity risk. Mitigation is daily backups of cloud storage data plus disaster recovery and business continuity plans. Risk is formally classified across strategic, operational, financial, commercial, sustainability, ESG and cyber security areas.

The cautionary statement warns that statements on future prospects involve identified and unidentified risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially, including changes in the macro-environment and events such as a global pandemic, and that the estimates rest on assumptions subject to change.

risks.risk: Subsidiary-level leverage and expansion at Apple Chemie
risks.note: While Indigo Paints is a zero-debt company on a standalone basis, the consolidated accounts carry debt pertaining to Apple Chemie India Private Limited, a majority of which relates to setting up an additional manufacturing facility at Nagpur and to working capital. The parent has also extended a guarantee to the subsidiary, so subsidiary execution and working-capital risk reaches the parent.

one-line thesis: Despite near-zero top-line growth in FY25 due to industry-wide sluggishness, Indigo Paints achieved record EBITDA and PAT margins through premiumization, cost discipline, and A&P efficiency; demand recovery in Q1FY26 and upcoming capacity commissioning in Q3FY26 position the company for a return to double-digit growth with margin expansion.
financial scorecard: revenue: +0.3% YoY (Q4), +1.8% YoY (FY25); EBITDA/margin: +4.4% YoY (Q4), 23.4% (record), FY25 EBITDA -0.5% to 231.6cr, margin 18.1%; PAT (rptd): +6.3% YoY (Q4) to 56.9cr, FY25 PAT -5.5% to 143.9cr; PAT (normalized): no material one-offs; order book: not disclosed; net debt: net cash position (no borrowings, rising treasury)
guidance: revenue growth: expected double-digit in FY26; margin: EBITDA margin to expand due to softer raw materials, improved mix, reduced trade discounts; order inflow: not specified; capex/commissioning: water-based plant Q3FY26, solvent-based plant Q1/Q2FY26, putty expansion end-Q1FY26
segment / subsidiary detail: Emulsion: value growth +1.3% in Q4 despite volume decline (premiumization); Enamel & Primer-Distemper: volume growth recovered in Q4; Putty: -1.3% value growth (low-margin, competitive); Waterproofing & Construction Chemicals: mid-single digit revenue contributor; Apple Chemie: +8.3% Q4 revenue growth, margins improving from Q3 lows
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion of dealer network (targeting 18,700+ active dealers), increased tinting machine adoption, institutional channel via Apple Chemie (B2B construction chemicals), premium product portfolio growth, and potential market share gains as industry recovers
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin: 47.4% in Q4 (industry-leading); EBITDA margin: 23.4% in Q4 (all-time high); Cost drivers: raw materials (emulsion monomers, alkyd resins) softening; freight costs declining due to southern plant commissioning and premiumization (higher value/kg reduces freight %); trade discounts rising in FY25 but now being moderated; A&P spend down to 5.0% of revenue in Q4 (from 6.3% YoY)
capex / expansion: Jodhpur water-based paint plant: commissioning Q3FY26 (delayed from Q2); solvent-based plant: commissioning end-Q1/Q2FY26; brownfield putty expansion: end-Q1FY26; total capex for FY26: not disclosed but implied to be modest and fully funded by cash flows
capital allocation: Dividend: Rs. 3.50/share recommended for FY25; no debt, strong cash generation; treasury surplus growing; no buybacks or M&A mentioned; capex funded internally; focus on organic growth and working capital efficiency
risks & watch-items: Monsoon delay in painting activity (early June 2025); geopolitical disruption affecting labor mobility (Punjab/J&K); potential titanium dioxide antidumping duty impact (judgment pending); competitive trade discounting in weak demand; Kerala market stagnation; slow recovery in Tier III/IV demand
management quality / tone: Confident and optimistic; acknowledges FY25 challenges but highlights record margins, disciplined cost control, and clear recovery signals in Q1FY26; management expects double-digit growth by Q2FY26; tone is assertive on premiumization and dealer expansion as core levers; dismissive of new entrant threat
non-obvious takeaways: Dealer count declined from 18,700 to 18,370 in FY25 due to market sluggishness — but management reports strong rebound in last 2 months, implying near-term volume catalyst; tinting machine adoption slowed in Q3-Q4 but accelerating again; 25,000+ painter families covered under health program — creates sticky loyalty and indirect sales channel; Apple Chemie’s B2B growth is a hidden growth engine not reflected in Indigo’s core paint numbers

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Indigo Paints Limited, incorporated in 2000 and headquartered in Pune, manufactures and sells decorative paints and allied products in India. Its portfolio spans interior and exterior emulsions, enamels, wood coatings, primers, putties, distempers, cement paints, waterproofing solutions and construction chemicals, serving residential, commercial and institutional requirements. Products reach the market through an expanding dealer network, depot infrastructure and an installed tinting-machine base, supported by manufacturing facilities in Rajasthan, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

growth_optionality.body: Expansion of dealer network (targeting 18,700+ active dealers), increased tinting machine adoption, institutional channel via Apple Chemie (B2B construction chemicals), premium product portfolio growth, and potential market share gains as industry recovers

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The year unfolded in two phases: a challenging first half with subdued industry demand and heightened competitive intensity, followed by a meaningful industry recovery from November 2025 onwards and renewed momentum across the business
- All four product categories recorded growth in both volume and value during the year, reflecting improving demand across the portfolio
- Gross margin improved to 46.9% on a standalone basis, supported by favourable product mix and operational discipline, even as raw material cost pressures were navigated towards the end of the year
- Policy tailwinds: reductions in the RBI policy repo rate eased borrowing conditions and improved housing affordability, while GST rationalisation and sustained government focus on housing and infrastructure supported construction activity; headline inflation moderated to 3.4%
- Real GDP is projected to grow 6.6% in FY2026-27, with continued government infrastructure spending, improving private investment and healthy consumption expected to support building-materials demand
- India's paints and coatings market was valued at approximately $9.4 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach nearly $17.7 billion by 2034, a CAGR of about 7.06%
- The Indian decorative paints market reached around $6.8 billion in FY2025-26, with growth expected from urbanisation, expanding residential construction and deeper penetration of organised paint products across Tier II and Tier III cities
- The Indian construction chemicals market is estimated at approximately $4.64 billion in 2025, projected to reach nearly $6.41 billion by 2035 (CAGR around 3.65%); the waterproofing market is projected to grow from about $1.27 billion in 2025 to over $1.94 billion by 2031 (CAGR around 7.31%)
- Premiumisation - rising preference for premium emulsions, specialised finishes and differentiated coatings - is the stated value-growth lever, alongside repainting/renovation demand and infrastructure-linked coatings
- Management expects Indigo Paints to enter a phase of stronger free cash flow generation from FY27 onwards as the investment cycle completes
- Challenges flagged: intensifying competition from new entrants and capacity expansion by established players, raw material price volatility in crude-linked derivatives, pigments and specialty chemicals, channel management complexity, and weather/demand cyclicality

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin: 47.4% in Q4 (industry-leading); EBITDA margin: 23.4% in Q4 (all-time high); Cost drivers: raw materials (emulsion monomers, alkyd resins) softening; freight costs declining due to southern plant commissioning and premiumization (higher value/kg reduces freight %); trade discounts rising in FY25 but now being moderated; A&P spend down to 5.0% of revenue in Q4 (from 6.3% YoY)

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Dividend: Rs. 3.50/share recommended for FY25; no debt, strong cash generation; treasury surplus growing; no buybacks or M&A mentioned; capex funded internally; focus on organic growth and working capital efficiency

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The capacity augmentation programme has been substantially completed. Two major capacity initiatives were finished during FY26 at Jodhpur, Rajasthan: a new solvent-based paint facility with a capacity of 12,000 KLPA was commissioned during FY2025-26, and putty manufacturing capacity was doubled from 1,38,000 MT to 2,76,000 MT. The remaining project is the Jodhpur water-based paint facility, which was in the final stages of commissioning at year-end with trial production scheduled to commence in H1 FY2026-27; the Company states that with the commissioning of the water-based plant it will have sufficient capacity to meet growing demand in the near future, and expects the facility to enhance manufacturing flexibility, improve service levels and support growth across northern and eastern markets. On the business-model page the Company sets out existing capacity of 1,72,000 KLPA plus 2,76,000 MTPA, rising to 2,62,000 KLPA plus 2,76,000 MTPA with new launches. The footprint stands at 6 manufacturing plants (existing plants shown at Kochi in Kerala, Pudukkottai in Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan, with Jodhpur marked as the upcoming plant), 55 depots and presence across 36 states and union territories. Beyond paints, subsidiary Apple Chemie India Pvt. Ltd. commissioned a new sealant manufacturing facility at Nagpur during FY2025-26, expanding the specialised construction chemicals platform for institutional, infrastructure and industrial customers. Management states the Company is well positioned to support future demand without significant near-term capital expenditure. On the sustainability side, BRSR Principle 2 reports that 1.67% of total capex in FY2025-26 went into technologies improving environmental and social impacts, against nil in FY2024-25, attributed to 330 kW of solar energy installed at the Kochi facility.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and optimistic; acknowledges FY25 challenges but highlights record margins, disciplined cost control, and clear recovery signals in Q1FY26; management expects double-digit growth by Q2FY26; tone is assertive on premiumization and dealer expansion as core levers; dismissive of new entrant threat

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Differentiated, category-first portfolio - described as India's first metallic paint, India's first floor coat paint, a first-of-its-kind tile coat paint and a unique ceiling coat paint - which the Company credits for holding the pole position on gross margin in the industry
- Gross margin reaching 46.9% in FY26, attributed to the basket of differentiated products and a prudent material purchase policy
- Distribution reach of 19,352 active dealers, 55 depots and 12,129 installed tinting machines, all expanded during FY26, plus 16 Indigo Colour Canvas experiential stores
- Sustained brand communication has made products such as PU Enamel, Floor Coat, Tile Coat and Dirtproof and Waterproof Exterior Laminate strongly associated with the Indigo brand
- Zero-debt on a standalone basis, with the only consolidated borrowing sitting at subsidiary Apple Chemie India Private Limited
- Broadened building-solutions platform through the majority stake in Apple Chemie, adding waterproofing and construction chemicals capability and institutional/infrastructure customer reach

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Monsoon delay in painting activity (early June 2025); geopolitical disruption affecting labor mobility (Punjab/J&K); potential titanium dioxide antidumping duty impact (judgment pending); competitive trade discounting in weak demand; Kerala market stagnation; slow recovery in Tier III/IV demand

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Dealer count declined from 18,700 to 18,370 in FY25 due to market sluggishness — but management reports strong rebound in last 2 months, implying near-term volume catalyst; tinting machine adoption slowed in Q3-Q4 but accelerating again; 25,000+ painter families covered under health program — creates sticky loyalty and indirect sales channel; Apple Chemie’s B2B growth is a hidden growth engine not reflected in Indigo’s core paint numbers

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Capture market opportunities: accelerate growth and strengthen competitive position through sharper market execution, wider product adoption and expanding presence across priority markets, with the stated aim of growing ahead of the market in FY2026-27
- Scale high-potential categories: raise the contribution from premium paints, waterproofing and construction chemicals by improving product adoption and scaling differentiated, application-led solutions
- Drive network productivity: increase throughput and wallet share across the active dealer network through better portfolio availability, …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Berger Paints outperformed Indigo in Q3-Q4 FY25 growth | Berger Paints | loser | Low | Indigo’s growth lag is regional (Kerala, weaker eastern presence), not structural; Indigo expects to outperform as demand recovers uniformly |
| New entrant claims 10% market share including putty | New Entrant (unspecified) | loser | Low | Management dismisses impact; no margin erosion observed; putty inclusion distorts comparison |
| Government MSME payment mandate reduced payables days | MSME Suppliers | beneficiary | Med | Indigo now pays MSMEs within 45 days — improves supplier relations but reduces working capital flexibility |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body: - [Outlook-Apple Chemie] Apple Chemie's Q1 FY27 revenue grew to Rs 19.7 Cr from Rs 14.0 Cr YoY, but margins were pressured by rising input costs and inventory buildup; gross margins expected to improve in Q2 FY27 and normalize by Q3 FY27.
